Krakow Podgorze Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kraków, Poland

Not demolished. This cemetery, established by the Jewish community of Podgórze in 1888, hosted a WWI military cemetery within its grounds, where 19 soldiers of the Austro-Hungarian army were buried. In 1941, the Germans closed the cemetery, and in 1942 established the Płaszów forced labor camp on the site, documented at the adjacent cemetery elsewhere in this collection; barracks were built there, and the funeral house was converted into a bathhouse. During the March 1943 liquidation of the Kraków Ghetto, victims were buried at the cemetery, and executions were also carried out there; in 1944, the Germans burned bodies from a mass grave. A single intact matzevah survives, commemorating Chaim Jakub Abrahamer, who died May 25, 1932.
